requirements.requirement: The application shall generate synthetic heart rate and oxygen saturation readings once per second during an active simulation.
requirements.srs_acceptance: A controlled 10-second simulation produces 10 scheduled reading sets.
requirements.rtm_acceptance: A controlled 10-second simulation produces 10 scheduled reading sets.

requirements.requirement: The frontend shall display each accepted reading within one second of receipt.
requirements.srs_acceptance: An automated integration test verifies the displayed value and elapsed time.
requirements.rtm_acceptance: An automated integration test verifies the displayed value and elapsed time.

requirements.requirement: Each displayed measurement shall include its name, value, unit, and measurement timestamp.
requirements.srs_acceptance: Heart rate displays in bpm; oxygen saturation displays in percent; timestamps match accepted readings.
requirements.rtm_acceptance: Heart rate displays in bpm; oxygen saturation displays in percent; timestamps match accepted readings.

requirements.requirement: The application shall accept finite numeric heart rate values from 0–300 bpm and oxygen saturation values from 0–100%, inclusive. These ranges are simulation input limits.
requirements.srs_acceptance: Boundary values are accepted; out-of-range, missing, nonnumeric, and nonfinite values are rejected.
requirements.rtm_acceptance: Boundary values are accepted; out-of-range, missing, nonnumeric, and nonfinite values are rejected.

requirements.requirement: Invalid readings shall not replace the last valid measurement. The frontend shall indicate invalid input, and the application shall record the rejection.
requirements.srs_acceptance: Injecting an invalid reading preserves the last valid value and creates a rejection event.
requirements.rtm_acceptance: Injecting an invalid reading preserves the last valid value and creates a rejection event.

requirements.requirement: The application shall activate a low-oxygen alarm after three consecutive valid readings below 92%. This threshold is a demonstration setting.
requirements.srs_acceptance: Two readings below 92% do not activate the alarm; the third activates it. A value of exactly 92% is not low.
requirements.rtm_acceptance: Two readings below 92% do not activate the alarm; the third activates it. A value of exactly 92% is not low.

requirements.requirement: A valid oxygen reading at or above 92%, an invalid oxygen reading, or a sensor disconnect shall reset the pending low-oxygen count.
requirements.srs_acceptance: Each reset condition requires three new consecutive low readings before activation.
requirements.rtm_acceptance: Each reset condition requires three new consecutive low readings before activation.

requirements.requirement: An active low-oxygen alarm shall clear after three consecutive valid oxygen readings at or above 92%. Invalid readings shall reset the recovery count.
requirements.srs_acceptance: Two qualifying recovery readings leave the alarm active; the third clears it.
requirements.rtm_acceptance: Two qualifying recovery readings leave the alarm active; the third clears it.

requirements.requirement: The user shall be able to acknowledge an active alarm. Acknowledgment shall change its status without clearing the underlying condition.
requirements.srs_acceptance: After acknowledgment, the alarm remains visible as active and acknowledged until its clearance criteria are met.
requirements.rtm_acceptance: After acknowledgment, the alarm remains visible as active and acknowledged until its clearance criteria are met.

requirements.requirement: A newly activated alarm following clearance shall require a new acknowledgment.
requirements.srs_acceptance: A previous acknowledgment does not carry over to a later alarm episode.
requirements.rtm_acceptance: A previous acknowledgment does not carry over to a later alarm episode.

requirements.requirement: A measurement shall be marked stale when more than five seconds have elapsed since receipt of its last valid reading.
requirements.srs_acceptance: At exactly five seconds it remains current; after five seconds it is stale. Before the first valid reading, it displays “No data.”
requirements.rtm_acceptance: At exactly five seconds it remains current; after five seconds it is stale. Before the first valid reading, it displays “No data.”

requirements.requirement: The frontend shall identify a simulated sensor disconnect and shall preserve the last valid readings with stale indicators when applicable.
requirements.srs_acceptance: Disconnecting the sensor displays its disconnected state; measurements become stale according to FR-011.
requirements.rtm_acceptance: Disconnecting the sensor displays its disconnected state; measurements become stale according to FR-011.

requirements.requirement: The application shall record session start/stop, alarm activation, acknowledgment, clearance, invalid input, and sensor disconnect/reconnect events.
requirements.srs_acceptance: Each event contains a session identifier, event type, UTC timestamp, and relevant details.
requirements.rtm_acceptance: Each event contains a session identifier, event type, UTC timestamp, and relevant details.

requirements.requirement: The frontend shall display session events in chronological order.
requirements.srs_acceptance: A known event sequence appears in the expected order, including events with identical timestamps.
requirements.rtm_acceptance: A known event sequence appears in the expected order, including events with identical timestamps.

requirements.requirement: The application shall reject readings whose measurement timestamp is equal to or earlier than the last accepted timestamp for that measurement.
requirements.srs_acceptance: Duplicate and older readings do not update displayed values or alarm counters and produce rejection events.
requirements.rtm_acceptance: Duplicate and older readings do not update displayed values or alarm counters and produce rejection events.

requirements.requirement: Starting a new session shall reset displayed readings, alarm states, and pending counters while retaining prior session records.
requirements.srs_acceptance: A new session begins with “No data” and no active alarms; previous events remain stored under their original session identifier.
requirements.rtm_acceptance: A new session begins with “No data” and no active alarms; previous events remain stored under their original session identifier.

requirements.srs_acceptance: Automated browser tests verify the notice is visible.
requirements.rtm_acceptance: Automated browser tests verify the notice is visible.

requirements.requirement: A missing scheduled SpO₂ reading interrupts consecutiveness and resets a pending activation or recovery counter; it does not clear an active alarm. A missed tick is detected using the deterministic simulation scheduler; the event is logged if storage is available. Verify low-low-gap-low does not activate, and recovery-recovery-gap-recovery does not clear.
requirements.rtm_acceptance: Verify specified behavior in TC-CL-001

requirements.requirement: Invalid physiological value, missing SpO₂ value, or malformed/missing measurement timestamp resets the applicable pending count; a duplicate/out-of-order timestamp, wrong session, or unauthorized input is rejected without changing alarm counters. None overwrite last accepted data. Each rejection is classified and tested.
requirements.rtm_acceptance: Verify specified behavior in TC-CL-002

requirements.requirement: The backend uses a monotonic clock for 5-second staleness and simulation deadlines, and UTC timestamps for records. At 5.000 s a reading is CURRENT; at >5.000 s it is STALE. UI delivery ≤1 second applies only while the authenticated browser connection is healthy under the specified controlled test environment; transport loss produces an immediate connection-uncertain indicator on detection.
requirements.rtm_acceptance: Verify specified behavior in TC-CL-003

requirements.requirement: Unexpected restart never resumes an old monitoring session or alarm episode automatically. UI shows monitoring stopped/restart detected; preserved event history is accessible only if storage is healthy; new session must be explicitly started. Verify with forced process termination and restart.
requirements.rtm_acceptance: Verify specified behavior in TC-CL-004

requirements.requirement: A monitoring-event write failure does not block alarm evaluation. The backend exposes event_storage_status=FAILED and history_completeness=INCOMPLETE; a subsequent successful write may restore write-health but must not claim that missing events were recovered. Verify failure and recovery behavior.
requirements.rtm_acceptance: Verify specified behavior in TC-CL-005

requirements.requirement: Network-mode operator commands that require accountable audit records (start/stop, acknowledge, sensor manipulation, security configuration) fail closed if the audit sink cannot accept a durable record, except an already-running sensor tick and automatic alarm evaluation must continue. The command response indicates failure without falsely reporting success; test audit-sink fault injection.
requirements.rtm_acceptance: Verify specified behavior in TC-CL-006

requirements.requirement: Local mode: bind 127.0.0.1 only; one explicit local-operator context, no remote access, visible mode banner; tests confirm external bind disabled. Network mode: secure authentication, Observer read-only, Operator authorized to start/stop/acknowledge and simulate sensor faults, session-level authorization for REST and WebSocket, origin and session checks, credential expiry/revocation handling.
requirements.rtm_acceptance: Verify specified behavior in TC-CL-007

requirements.requirement: Every authoritative state snapshot includes session_id, revision, server timestamp, sensor status, connection-independent data freshness, alarm episode/state, storage health and history completeness. Revision increases for each accepted mutation; clients discard older revisions and GET a fresh snapshot after reconnection.
requirements.rtm_acceptance: Verify specified behavior in TC-CL-008

requirements.requirement: In deterministic scheduler tests, a 10-second active simulation emits 10 scheduled sets, with exact fake-clock ticks. In controlled local browser integration tests, 95% of accepted readings must render within 1.0 second of backend acceptance with no injected delay; all timing exceptions are logged and reviewed. This is a project target, not clinical performance validation.
requirements.rtm_acceptance: Verify specified behavior in TC-CL-009

requirements.requirement: Record each processed field (including account ID, IP address, timestamps, audit metadata), purpose, access, retention, deletion and applicable jurisdiction. requirements.rtm_acceptance: Verify specified behavior in TC-CL-010
